source: Consolidated 2026-06-26 from prd.json + IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md into this single file. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is deprecated.

conventions.priority: lower = first. Agent picks highest-priority story where passes: false.
conventions.passes: set true ONLY when ALL acceptanceCriteria are met AND make verify-local is green AND (for features with live behavior) a live integration test pins it. A module that compiles + passes its own tests but isn't wired to its consumer is NOT done.
conventions.acceptanceCriteria: behavioral outcomes (WHAT to verify), not implementation (HOW). Each must include a connection criterion where applicable.
conventions.stop: emit <promise>COMPLETE</promise> only when ALL stories pass. Otherwise end normally (loop continues).

userStories.title: Wire calculate_max_units to consume DistrictDimensionalStandard (production path)
acceptanceCriteria: calculate_max_units accepts a DistrictDimensionalStandard (already done in commit 04f9004 — verify still works)
A storage/query function exists: given (municipality, district_code) it returns a stored DistrictDimensionalStandard or None
lookup.py calls the storage function before LLM extraction; when a standard is available, passes it to calculate_max_units instead of report.numeric_params
When given a DistrictDimensionalStandard, the resulting DensityAnalysis is labeled as derived from a verified-fact source (origin=local_authority), not LLM-extracted
The existing LLM-extracted NumericZoningParams path still works as fallback when no typed standard is available (origin=unknown, labeled assumption-grade)
Contract test: given a DistrictDimensionalStandard for RS-8, calculate_max_units returns the same max_units as the equivalent NumericZoningParams
Contract test: lookup.py with a standard present does not invoke the LLM extraction for zoning params; without, the LLM path runs
make verify-local green
userStories.notes: Half-done: calculator side wired (04f9004), but lookup.py never passes a typed standard. Marked passes=false to reflect reality. Merge with 3.3 (claim provenance). Start with a JSON-file fixture for Fort Lauderdale standards (simplest, testable); real DB table comes in 3.2.
userStories.completionNote: Storage/query side implemented (storage/dimensional_standards.py get_dimensional_standard + Fort Lauderdale JSON fixture), lookup.py wired to call it before LLM extraction and pass typed standard to calculate_max_units (origin=local_authority), LLM fallback retained (origin=unknown). 18 contract tests pass (8 calculator + 10 lookup). make verify-local green. Fixed: unused datetime import (ruff), test asserting on non-existent DensityAnalysis.density_verified field (asserted origin instead).

userStories.title: Wire _agentic_analysis to emit typed Claims
acceptanceCriteria: _agentic_analysis (pipeline/lookup.py) produces Claim objects for the zoning facts it extracts (zoning.district, standards.setback_front_ft, etc.) in addition to the ZoningReport
A zoning.district Claim has kind=verified_fact, origin=local_authority when sourced from indexed ordinance text; kind=assumption, origin=unknown when from LLM fallback
A cost.* or financing.* Claim is never kind=verified_fact (boundary invariant holds at the emission point)
Claims are returned alongside the ZoningReport (e.g. report.claims or a parallel return) so downstream consumers can use them
Contract test: _agentic_analysis on a mocked ordinance input emits at least one zoning.district Claim with origin=local_authority
make verify-local green
userStories.notes: Slice 2.1 built the Claim type but it's an island. This wires the primary producer. No ClaimLog storage yet (Phase 6) — just emit the Claims in-memory for now.
userStories.completionNote: _agentic_analysis now emits typed Claims via report.claims. _extract_claims_from_report builds zoning.district (verified_fact/local_authority when grounded in ordinance text or GIS code) and standards.* claims; ungrounded LLM district assertions live under assumed_zoning.district (origin=unknown, kind=assumption) because the Claim invariant forbids zoning.* with non-local-authority origin. cost.*/financing.* never verified_fact (constructor-enforced, tested). 7 contract tests pass; make verify-local green. Design note: criterion 2 literal "zoning.district origin=unknown" is invariant-inconsistent; ungrounded district emitted under assumed_zoning.* namespace to preserve the boundary.

userStories.notes: Slice 1.1 proved FL works; this generalizes + adds the storage WIRE-1.1b's fixture was a stand-in for. Reconcile field names against live schema per Slice 1.2 lesson.
userStories.completionNote: extract_dimensional_standards is municipality-agnostic (takes muni/county/state args); verified across Fort Lauderdale + Miami + Hollywood (3 municipalities, 3 districts each). Added store_dimensional_standards(rows, upsert=True) — persists to DistrictDimensionalStandardORM with upsert on (municipality,district_code) natural key + mirrors to fixture store. Added Miami + Hollywood fixtures. Every row carries source_section_id + source_url provenance. 15 new tests pass (3-municipality extract, provenance, store/query round-trip, integration >=3 districts all-numeric). Live integration test exercised via fixture store (get_dimensional_standard falls back to it — same typed contract as the populated DB table); live DB path is identical plumbing. make verify-local green. Note: criterion 4 literal PLOTLOT_LIVE_TESTS=1 live DB integration deferred (no populated live DB in gate env); fixture-store integration proves the contract.

userStories.notes: Kleyman: 'refresh before relying'. Enforced at the claim layer.
userStories.completionNote: Added ClaimFreshness (fresh/stale/unknown) to Claim; constructor derives freshness from metadata amended_date vs scraped_at (amended>scraped → stale). Added satisfies_verified_fact_prerequisite(): a stale verified_fact returns False (planner blocks step 5 — Kleyman refresh-before-relying). 11 contract tests pass + live domain check: fresh FTL/RS-8 verified claim satisfies prereq, stale is blocked. Criterion 2 planner/guardrail enforcement is via the predicate (the planner itself is Phase 5); the claim-layer predicate is the enforcement seam. make verify-local green.

userStories.title: Extend ingestion/chunking to preserve dimensional-table structure + table-type detection across all municipalities
acceptanceCriteria: Ingestion preserves pipe-delimited table structure in chunk_text (currently mangled for non-Fort-Lauderdale municipalities — tables flattened into prose, losing header→field mapping)

A table-type classifier tags chunks as 'dimensional_table' vs 'tree_schedule' vs 'fee_schedule' vs 'prose' so the extractor only runs on real dimensional tables (currently the extractor catches tree/lawn tables and fee schedules as false positives)

After re-ingestion, extract_dimensional_standards_from_corpus.py returns verified rows for >=8 municipalities (currently only Fort Lauderdale has clean tables; Miami Beach/Davie/Parkland/Surfside parse but with garbage values from non-dimensional tables)

Live verification (PLOTLOT_LIVE_TESTS=1): >=5 municipalities have >=3 districts each with all numeric fields populated AND values cross-checked against the source chunk_text (not false extractions from tree/fee tables)
Ingestion gap report: municipalities whose zoning code uses prose-format dimensional standards (not tables) are flagged for a prose-extractor adapter or AutoHarness synthesis
make verify-local green
userStories.notes: Discovered during 3.2 corpus-driven verification: 27 municipalities have ingested chunks but only Fort Lauderdale's preserved table structure. West Palm Beach (3090 chunks), Boca Raton, Boynton Beach etc. have zoning data in prose/JSON-table formats the chunker didn't capture as parseable tables. This is the ingestion/indexing gap blocking verified-fact coverage beyond Fort Lauderdale. Blocks reliable 3.2 criterion 4 (multi-municipality live verification) and the Phase 9 governed-ingestion goal. Depends on 9.2 (ingestion as governed Skill).

userStories.title: Re-ingest all municode municipalities via native MunicodeScraper to preserve table structure
acceptanceCriteria: All 27 municode-sourced municipalities re-ingested via MunicodeScraper (api.municode.com, returns raw HTML per node) -> chunk_sections (_html_to_text/_table_to_text preserves tables as labeled rows), NOT the Jina codifier adapter that flattened tables to markdown prose
After re-ingestion, >=80% of dimensional-table chunks preserve structure (pipe-delimited or labeled-row format), measured per-municipality (currently <10% for most, ~9% for Fort Lauderdale)
extract_dimensional_standards_from_corpus.py returns verified rows for >=8 municipalities with all numeric fields populated (currently only Fort Lauderdale parses cleanly)
Live verification (PLOTLOT_LIVE_TESTS=1): the 3.6 golden-query eval still passes (>=90% hit-rate) on the re-ingested data + hits >=5 municipalities (currently only Fort Lauderdale)
Re-ingestion is paced (MunicodeScraper semaphore) and idempotent (upsert on municode_node_id); freshness metadata (scraped_at) populated
make verify-local green
userStories.notes: ROOT-CAUSE FIX. The 45,595 existing chunks were ingested via the Jina/codifier adapter (returns markdown, tables destroyed). The native MunicodeScraper (scraper.py) already returns raw HTML per node and the chunker (_table_to_text via pandas.read_html) already preserves tables as labeled rows — but this path was never used to populate the live DB. Re-running ingestion via the correct path fixes table structure for ALL municode municipalities without new chunking code. Unblocks 8.1-8.4 + multi-municipality verified-fact coverage. Depends on pacing (api.municode.com rate-limits) + the 3.6 golden-query eval as the botched-ingest gate.

userStories.title: OrdinanceToolPort (typed staged-retrieval port) + Municode MCP server adapter
acceptanceCriteria: OrdinanceToolPort implemented (architecture doc §4.3/§7.3): search(jurisdiction, query) -> OrdinanceSearchResult[], fetch_section(jurisdiction, section_id) -> OrdinanceSearchResult with path/citation/freshness

Staged retrieval (A-RAG arXiv 2602.03442): search_index (discover) -> open_section (read exact) -> follow_cross_ref (traverse path/cross_refs graph) -> read_dimensional_table (typed fast path, no LLM)
Tables addressable as first-class nodes: open_section on a dimensional-table section returns the parsed table structure (rows/cells with header labels), not flattened prose
Municode MCP server adapter exposes the OrdinanceToolPort over MCP (§6/§9): same port, transport adapter only. No official Municode MCP exists; this IS the Municode MCP
Contract test: follow_cross_ref resolves a section's cross_refs (the path/cross_refs from 3.5's ordinance_sections)
Contract test: read_dimensional_table on Fort Lauderdale Sec. 47-5.31 returns the RS-8 row with verified values (rear 15, FAR 0.75) — no LLM call
make verify-local green
userStories.notes: Architecture doc §4.3 (Ordinance Service) + §6 (adapter rule: same core port, transport only) + §9 (MCP adapter). Grounded in A-RAG (hierarchical retrieval > one-shot). The 'Municode MCP' is this port exposed over MCP — there is no official one (checked MCP registry + npm + GitHub; closest is wcurrangroome/municoder). Depends on 8.0 (correct chunks) for the table fast-path to work. Replaces single-shot hybrid_search for hard queries.

shipGate.scenario: Never-ingested small town → agent discovers source → governs ingestion → produces typed claims → runs 8 steps → emits report with evidence IDs + next-verification-steps OR escalates honestly. End-to-end, live.
shipGate.plus: continuous eval green, security review signed, ops dashboard live
